assumptions: the 162 rules proved terminating in EXP-C04-01
exhaustive derivation graphs from all words of length <= 12 (<= 8 for four exponential rules, extended to 20 by a verified formula)
meta.falsification: A rule whose D_max admits no over-determined recurrence, or a growth class other than linear/quadratic/exponential.
meta.hypothesis: H-C04-G: every terminating rule in the family has derivational complexity D(n) = max over words of length n of the longest derivation that is linear, quadratic or exponential, and D(n) is given by a linear recurrence (rational generating function).
meta.methodology: Exact min/max derivation lengths per word from the acyclic derivation graph; D_max(n), D_min(n); minimal linear recurrence (Berlekamp-Massey, over-determined) and the moduli/multiplicities of its characteristic roots give the growth class. Rules are grouped by the symmetries reversal and letter exchange.
meta.question: How long can derivations of a terminating one-rule system be, as a function of the length of the start word, and which growth classes occur?
meta.title: Derivational complexity of terminating one-rule systems (|l|, |r| <= 3)

summary: 162 terminating rules in 55 symmetry classes; growth classes (rules): {'linear': 140, 'quadratic': 14, 'exponential': 4, 'no recurrence found': 4}
